conventions.event_names: Exactly the names in `events`. UPPER_SNAKE, no suffix. A game never invents new event names.
conventions.parameter_keys: Exactly the keys listed for the state, UPPER_SNAKE. Pattern keys (BALANCE_<CURRENCY>, POWERUP_<NAME>) are the only generated keys.
conventions.state: Every event has STATE. Never STAGE, STATUS, or a value used as a key.
conventions.closed_enums: Values listed in an `enum` are PascalCase and exactly as written.
conventions.game_ids: Game vocabulary (placements, screens, tutorials, powerups, currencies, level IDs) is lower_snake, built with the naming rules.
conventions.product_ids: The raw store product ID, unchanged.
conventions.types: int, float, string, bool. bool is sent as int 0 or 1.
conventions.unknown: Omit the parameter. Never send None, none, null, unknown or an empty string.
conventions.lists: Never several values in one parameter.
conventions.personal_data: Never player names, emails or any text the player typed.

STATE.note: One of the states listed for the event.

LEVEL_NUMBER.note: 1-based player-facing level the event concerns. On every event when the game has a current level.

naming_rules.lower_snake: Take the code identifier, drop suffixes Screen, Panel, Popup, Window, View, Controller, Manager, Button; split CamelCase and digits; lowercase; join with _. Example: RemoveAdsSubPanel -> remove_ads_sub.
naming_rules.screens: Use these names when the game has the screen: main_menu, shop, settings, leaderboard, profile, spin_wheel, daily_gift, remove_ads, no_internet, item_unlock, powerup_popup, rate_us. Otherwise apply lower_snake.
naming_rules.tutorials: first_level for the first-play tutorial; powerup_<powerup> for a powerup tutorial; feature_<name> for any other feature tutorial.
naming_rules.placements: <where>_<what>: level_complete_x2, level_fail_revive, level_skip, powerup_<powerup>, shop_coins, daily_gift_x2, spin_wheel_extra, app_open, level_interstitial, unattributed.
naming_rules.powerups: lower_snake of the powerup type: extra_slot, shuffle, bomb, rockets, auto_shoot.

tiers.core: LEVEL, AD, ECONOMY, APP. Ship first.
tiers.standard: TUTORIAL, FTUE, POWERUP, SCREEN, IAP, PLAYER.

LEVEL.purpose: One attempt at a level, joined by ATTEMPT_ID.

Started.trigger: The board is playable and the player can act.

ATTEMPT.note: How many times this player started this level, including this one.

LEVEL_ID.note: Content ID when levels loop or are reordered.

Started.extras: Up to 5 game-specific parameters (UPPER_SNAKE, scalar) may be added here only, and must be listed in the report.

Completed.trigger: The player wins, before result animations or ads.

Failed.trigger: The player loses, before result animations or ads.

Skipped.trigger: The player skips the level (paid, ad or free).

Restarted.trigger: The player restarts the level from inside it (pause or settings menu).

Left.trigger: The attempt ends without a result.

RECOVERED.note: 1 when sent on the next launch for an attempt the process died in.

Choice.trigger: The player picks what happens after a result.

ACTION.note: Abandoned: the app closed or died before a choice.

SECONDS.note: Active play; excludes background and fullscreen ads.

PROGRESS_PCT.note: 0-100 share of the level's goal done.

ADS_SHOWN.note: AD Show events during this attempt.

SKIP_OFFERED.note: 1 when the result screen offers a skip. Offers on the result screen are flags here, never their own events.

rules: Send each of Completed/Failed/Skipped at most once per result. A Revive continues the same attempt and may produce another result.
Backgrounding is not Left; APP Background and Foreground cover it.
Coins are never reported here; ECONOMY is the ledger.

AD.purpose: One ad attempt, joined by AD_ID. Revenue and impressions come from the ad plugin.

Show.trigger: Immediately before the provider show call.

Failed.trigger: No ad was shown when the game wanted one, including a rewarded button pressed with no ad loaded.

FALLBACK.note: 1 when an interstitial stands in for a rewarded ad.

rules: Show is not proof of an impression; a missing Closed is not proof of a crash.

ECONOMY.purpose: The ledger for every soft currency. The only place amounts appear.

SOURCE.note: Lower_snake closed set. gift covers daily gifts, spin wheels and chests.

DETAIL.note: lower_snake game detail, e.g. the powerup bought or the product.

APP.purpose: Process lifecycle. Never creates SDK sessions.

PREV_EXIT.note: How the previous run ended: clean quit, closed by the OS while in background, or died in foreground. Omitted on first launch.

Completed.trigger: The player does the prompted action.

Interrupted.trigger: Cancelled, lost its target or the app was left.

rules: Repeated hints after the tutorial is done are not new Shown events.

FTUE.purpose: First-run steps before the first player input, invisible to every other event.

Reached.trigger: A new install reaches a step for the first time.

STEP_INDEX.note: Fixed: loading_done=1, consent_done=2, board_visible=3, first_input=4, even when a step does not exist in the game.

rules: Once per install. Skip steps the game does not have; never renumber.
board_visible: the first level is drawn and accepts input. first_input: the first gameplay input.

SCREEN.purpose: Every menu and popup, one event name.

SOURCE.note: Previous screen name, or auto when the game opened it by itself.

Interaction.trigger: A meaningful button inside the screen.

ACTION.note: lower_snake of the button: play, buy, watch_ad, music_off.

ITEM.note: lower_snake item or store product ID.

Closed.trigger: The screen hides. Required for shop and offer popups; optional elsewhere.

rules: Gameplay and level result screens are covered by LEVEL and are never SCREEN events.

IAP.purpose: Store purchases, from existing store callbacks only.

Purchased.trigger: The store confirms a new sale.

Failed.trigger: The store reports failure or cancel.

rules: Restores, renewals and refunds are not sent.

PLAYER.purpose: The player's state, once per SDK session after load.

Snapshot.trigger: Once per session, after the save is loaded.

BALANCE_<CURRENCY>.note: One key per currency, e.g. BALANCE_COINS.

DEVICE.purpose: Hardware facts the SDK does not send.

Snapshot.trigger: Once per install and again when the app version or quality tier changes.

website.sdk_events: session_start, session_end and first_open come from the SDK and are never sent by the game.
derived: session number and session seconds (session_start and client_ts)
process runs (APP Launch ordered by seq)
time buckets and funnels over existing events
